title: Redwood Optimize: Model-Aware Batching v1.0 Product Requirements and Roadmap
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview:

Purpose: This document defines the Product Requirements, high-level design, roadmap, pricing and release notes for Redwood Optimize: Model-Aware Batching (MAB) v1.0 - a feature to reduce per-token cost and improve tail latency by dynamically selecting batching policies per-request and per-model. Target audiences: product, serving runtime, infra, SRE, applied ML, solutions engineering.

Summary: MAB v1.0 builds on the Optimize toolkit to provide: (1) runtime policy selection that adapts batch size to request distribution and model KV cache footprint, (2) per-customer configurable SLO profiles (latency vs cost), and (3) an opt-in A/B rollout with observability and rollback controls in Redwood Console. Expected impact: 15-35% token cost reduction for LLM workloads with modest latency improvements for CPU-bound small-sequence workloads and up to 20% tail-latency reduction for high-concurrency customers.

Goals and Non-Goals:

Goals:
- Deliver a production-first MAB feature that safely reduces per-token cost for hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Provide per-model and per-route policy inference and expose controls in Console.
- Ensure automated rollback and safety thresholds to avoid customer-visible QoS regressions.
- Instrumentation: Per-policy cost, latency P50/P95/P99, quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

Non-Goals for v1.0:
- Model parameter-level optimization (quantization logic) - that remains in Quantization Profiles.
- Private unattended deployments with custom kernel modifications; MAB will ship with supported runtime kernels only.

Product Requirements (PRD):

1) Functional Requirements
1.1 Runtime policy selection
- System must select batching policy per request based on: model family, request sequence length, presence/absence of KV prefix cache, and current GPU utilization.
- Supported policies: fixed-batch-size (n=1..16), adaptive-batching (latency budget input), prefix-aware merging, no-batching (pass-through).

1.2 Per-tenant SLO profiles
- Admins can configure three SLO tiers: latency_preferred, cost_preferred, balanced.
- Each tier maps to default policy parameters (e.g., target latency budget ms, max batch size, backpressure thresholds).

1.3 Observability and Telemetry
- Emit metrics: policy.selected, policy.batch_size, policy.queue_depth, policy.effective_tokens_per_second, policy.estimated_cost_savings.
- Log decision traces (lightweight) with sampling (1%) for debugging.

1.4 Safety and Rollback
- Automatic rollback triggers if real-time quality checks (eval prompt set) degrade by >2% for 10m window or latency SLO violations >5% of requests.
- Manual canary controls: % of traffic, model variants to route to, staged ramp.

1.5 Console UX
- Expose policy tuning UI: per-route sliders for latency vs cost, preview of estimated savings, and historical metrics visualization.
- A/B rollout panel with start/stop and percentage controls.

2) Non-Functional Requirements
- Latency overhead of policy decision must be <1ms median.
- CPU overhead per-host <= 3% of baseline.
- Backwards-compatible with existing API: defaults preserve current behavior when MAB is disabled.
- Security: decisions and telemetry must honor customer confidentiality and PII redaction rules.

3) Data and Quality Requirements
- Model-specific eval prompt-sets must be registered for quality regression checks.
- Minimum 30-day history retention for per-policy cost and latency metrics in Console for analysis (configurable for enterprise).

Design Overview and Key Decisions:

High-level design:
- Decision service: a lightweight, local-inference module embedded in the runtime agent selects policies for each request. The module consults a policy table and runtime signals (gpu_util, queue_depth, seq_len) to return a policy token used by the batching layer.
- Batching layer: implements policy semantics (merge heuristics, batch size limits, prefix-aware KV grouping).
- Control plane: Console-hosted policy editor and rollout manager; policies stored in central config and pushed to runtime agents via existing config distribution pipeline.

Important design decisions:
- Local decision service vs remote: chosen local to satisfy latency SLO and offline operation in Private deployments.
- Sampling of decision traces set to 1% by default to limit telemetry volume.
- Policy table modeled as flat rules to simplify rollout and diffing.

Implementation Plan and Timeline (Roadmap & Themes):

Q4 2025 (Discovery & Spike) - complete
- Measurement spike across top 20 customers to quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Define policy feature set and evaluate safe thresholds.

Q1 2026 (MVP Implementation) - completed
- Implement local decision module and basic fixed/adaptive batching policies.
- Add policy telemetry and Console preview panel.
- Internal dogfood with 3 internal services and 2 pilot customers.

Q2 2026 (Canary + Observability) - completed
- Expand canary to 10% of traffic for pilot customers.
- Add automatic rollback triggers and quality alerting tied to eval prompt sets.

Q3 2026 (v1.0 GA) - planned release 2026-09-15
- GA for Hosted API and Dedicated customers.
- Console: per-route policy editor, A/B rollout, historical metrics.
- Pricing/packaging published.

Q4 2026 (Enterprise & Private Enhancements) - planned
- Private deployment packaging, tighter KMS/HSM integration of telemetry, 90-day configurable storage for enterprise customers, and improved per-model heuristics.

Prioritization Themes:
- Safety-first: any policy must have automated fallback and must preserve deterministic behavior when configured.
- Observability: users must be able to quantify savings and quality impact with minimal effort.
- Low-friction adoption: default config should be opt-in with a clear rollback story.

Pricing and Packaging Notes:

Overview: MAB will be included as part of Redwood Optimize add-on. Pricing model balances unit economics and value capture.

Tiers (suggested):
- Optimize Basic (included): policy recommendations only in Console (no runtime automation).
- Optimize MAB Standard (add-on): runtime policy automation for Hosted APIs and Dedicated; 10% surcharge on existing token pricing but with expected 15-25% net cost savings for customers that enable the feature.
- Optimize MAB Enterprise: includes private deployment support, extended metric retention, SLA-backed rollout assistance; custom pricing (annual contract).

Billing mechanics:
- For Standard, surcharge applies to requests where MAB policy deviates from baseline batching behavior. We will report gross_savings_estimate and net_charge in billing reports for transparency.
- Free trial: 30-day free trial for new customers on Optimize Standard during Q3 2026 GA window.

Pricing rationale and examples:
- Example customer A: mid-market SaaS, $10k monthly token spend. Expected savings 20% => $2k savings, surcharge 10% on enabled traffic (~$1k) => net customer savings ~$1k/month.
- Example customer B: high-SLO enterprise with low willingness to risk quality - likely choose Optimize Basic or Enterprise.

Release Notes (v1.0 GA) - 2026-09-15:

Highlights:
- GA: Model-Aware Batching v1.0 for Hosted API + Dedicated.
- Console: per-route policy editor, A/B rollout controls, historical metrics and savings preview.
- Automatic rollback thresholds based on quality evals and latency SLOs.

Fixed and Improvements:
- Reduced per-token CPU overhead by optimizing decision module to C++ shim (median decision latency 0.6ms).
- Improved batching heuristics to avoid prefix cache thrashing for autoregressive decoding.

Known Limitations and Future Work:
- Private on-prem packaging requires additional runtime testing for air-gapped scenarios (planned Q4 2026).
- Per-model micro-optimizations (e.g., kernel selection tied to batch composition) are deferred to a future release.

Rollout Plan and Operational Playbook:

Canary Phases:
1) Internal dogfood (complete) - 1 week, internal monitoring.
2) Pilot customers (complete) - 4 weeks, 5-10% traffic.
3) Gradual ramp (planned) - 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2-4 weeks with manual gates and automatic rollback.

Monitoring and Acceptance Criteria:
- No increase in quality regressions >1% on eval prompt sets during a 24h window.
- Latency P95 must not increase by more than 10% for latency_preferred customers.
- Cost savings estimate must be positive after surcharge for >=70% of pilot customers.

Operational runbook (high level):
- If automatic rollback triggers, on-call owner: eng-serving-runtime first responder.
- Steps: 1) Pause rollout in Console, 2) Revert to previous policy set, 3) Open incident in incident response queue, 4) Notify affected customers and CS lead, 5) Postmortem within 72 hours if rollback affects >1 customer.

Metrics and KPIs:
- Adoption rate (pct of eligible customers enabling MAB).
- Average cost savings per customer (net of surcharge).
- Latency P95/P99 delta for latency_preferred customers.
- Number of automatic rollbacks and root-cause categories.

Dependencies:
- Runtime: kernel and batching layer APIs must support policy tokens and prefix-aware grouping.
- Console: policy editor and rollout manager UI components.
- Billing: support for reporting net_charge and savings metadata.
- Applied ML: curated eval prompt sets per model.

Open Questions:
- Should we expose an advanced policy DSL for solutions engineering or keep policies opaque?
- What is the optimal surcharge cap for Standard to maximize adoption while preserving value capture?
- For private deployments, what telemetry can we feasibly collect without violating air-gap requirements?

Appendix: Examples and Config Snippets:

Example policy rule (illustrative text):
- name: low-latency-short-seq
- match: model-family: gptx-small, seq_len <= 64, kv_hit=false
- action: fixed_batch_size:1, max_wait_ms:5

CLI example (preview policy):
- redwood optimize policy preview --route /v1/generate --policy low-latency-short-seq --window 24h
